newsitem.title: ITALY: UN agency appeals for fertiliser for North Korea.
newsitem.headline: UN agency appeals for fertiliser for North Korea.

text.p: The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation on Monday launched an appeal to the international community to supply fertiliser to famine-threatened North Korea to boost rice crops.
The Rome-based FAO said in a statement that 50,000 tonnes of fertiliser costing some $11 million was needed for distribution in North Korea over the next six weeks.

"Through the delivery of fertiliser within the next six weeks and by latest July 25 for the present planting season, rice production could be increased by about 370,000 tonnes or 24 percent," FAO said.
Isolationist North Korea was hit by massive flooding in 1995 and 1996 which led to the devestation of cereal crops across the country.
The World Food Programme (WFP), the U.N. agency which plans emergency food aid distribution, cautioned after a visit last month that North Korea was within months of running out of food supplies.

The WFP launched a $95.5 million appeal earlier this year to purchase and deliver 203,000 tonnes of emergency food to North Korea. The United States has pledged $25 million and South Korea pledged $16 million in response to the appeal.
Both countries have said further large-scale aid must be tied to North Korea's participation in four-nation peace talks which would also include China.
